title: Bonsai microresponse playbook
content:
PERSONAL SCRATCHPAD - do not circulate without permission

Context / problem:
- Many customers (chat assistants, search assistants, task UIs) want fast, cheap initial answers for low friction tasks. Full responses are often overkill, increasing tokens and latency.
- Existing fallback/ladder strategies are coarse (short vs full) and often either lose clarity or still cost too much.

Idea: Bonsai microresponse- a tiny initial answer (1-3 sentences or a bullet) delivered from a low-cost model variant, optionally expand-on-demand into fuller answers.

Goals / success metrics:
- P50 initial-response latency <= 120ms (edge cached or tiny model).
- Reduce median tokens per session by 30% in flows where users accept initial microresponses.
- Maintain end-user satisfaction (NPS proxy or thumbs-up) within 5% of baseline.

How it works (high level):
1) Request arrives with hint parameter bonsai_hint: true or client preference bonsai_level: tiny|short|full.
2) Router routes to a lightweight model (quantized 7B or trimmed prompt path) for tiny/short.
3) Service returns microresponse + expansion handle token (expansion_id) and short provenance (source-meta).
4) If user taps expand, call expansion endpoint with expansion_id; route to full model and stitch cached context.

API sketch (proto):
- POST /v1/generate?bonsai_level=tiny
  body: { prompt, session_id, expand_on_idle: bool }
  response: { bonsai_text, expansion_id (optional), model_hint }

User stories:
- As a front-end PM, I want the assistant to show a one-line summary first so users can decide whether to expand.
- As a platform engineer, I want cheap route options to steer low-cost traffic without degrading fallbacks.
- As an SRE, I need observability for bonsai vs full requests (token counts, expansions, latencies).

Experiment design:
- A/B test: control (always full) vs treatment (bonsai-first). Measure expansion rate, task completion, token usage.
- Ramp rules: start on low-traffic cohorts, enable for read-only info queries first.

Operational details / optimizations:
- Cache microresponses by (normalized prompt fingerprint) for ~1h TTL to hit p50 latency.
- Prefetch expansion candidates (generate summary + plan) so expansion is fast (warm cache of KV cache).
- Use continuous-batching lane for expansions to amortize kernel cost.
- Cost policy: charge microresponse at lower unit rate; expansion billed separately.

UX considerations:
- Visual affordance: truncated preview with chevron, or inline bullets, and explicit "Show more" CTA.
- Safety: microresponse must not omit critical safety signals; ensure safety filter runs on micro and expansion.
- Explainability: include small provenance tag ("source: KB" / "model: M-mini-v1").

Risks / open questions:
- When will microresponse mislead because it omits disambiguating details? Can we detect and force full?
- Latency vs accuracy trade: how much do users tolerate being served by cheaper models?
- Billing complexity and UX for users who expand often.

TODOs / next steps:
- Spike: implement tiny-model route + minimal API surface (2 engineer-weeks).
- UX mock: Maya to draft 3 simple affordance options by next Wed.
- Metric hooks: add bonsai tag to existing telemetry events (INF-4821).
- Experiment spec: draft A/B in GH PR#678 and link to confluence page.

Notes / brainstorms (quick):
- variants: inline bonsai (within chat bubble), ephemeral tooltip, search snippet enrichment.
- gating heuristics: query length heuristics, intent classifier to prefer full for complex asks.
- possible name alternatives: "snap", "quickleaf", "microdigest" (I like Bonsai).

Unresolved:
- pricing model: subscription credit vs per-episode split?
- how to surface expansion cost to end-users (transparent vs bundled).

Reference links: JIRA INF-4821 (instrumentation), GH PR#678 (api proto), confluence/mini-response-patterns (early research).

Random notes: prototype should be cheap to iterate — start with server-side flag + UI experiment rather than new public API.

End of pad.
